findings.claim: The challenge terminal-status equality predicate lacks an independent negative control, as required by acceptance criterion 7.
findings.evidence: In test_challenge_terminal_and_closure, changing CurrentStatus to 0 leaves TerminalResolutionKind=0 and ClosedUtc populated. Even if the validator's history[-1]['Status'] == r['CurrentStatus'] check were removed, this case would still fail the open-wrapper closure-metadata checks. The later open-wrapper mutations do not isolate a status mismatch either: the TerminalResolutionKind mutation changes the wrapper and terminal disposition together to resolved. Thus the supplied tests do not demonstrate detection of a missing terminal-status equality guard.
findings.requestedFix: Add an otherwise-valid status-mismatch control. For example, construct an open wrapper with TerminalResolutionKind and ClosedUtc null, and a valid resolved terminal disposition whose ResolutionKind is nonnull and whose ChallengeResponseId is valid. This necessarily also mismatches terminal resolution, so additionally use a focused predicate-specific control or mutation control demonstrating that removal of the status-equality predicate is detected independently of the resolution-equality predicate. Retain public-API rejection coverage and document any structural coupling that prevents a single otherwise-valid public payload from isolating this predicate.

Within the stated closed public status domain {0,1}, a valid disposition is resolved exactly when ResolutionKind is nonnull, and a valid wrapper is resolved exactly when TerminalResolutionKind is nonnull. Equality of those resolution values therefore implies equality of terminal and wrapper statuses.

Consequently, an otherwise-valid public payload cannot violate only terminal-status equality. Removing only that comparison cannot change acceptance while the coupled guards remain intact. An implementation-mirroring predicate test is unnecessary to establish this public behavior.

The supplied parent evidence reports enumeration of all 256 combinations of two wrapper statuses, two entry statuses, four wrapper resolutions, four entry resolutions, closure presence, and response presence. It reports agreement across C#, current Python, and Python with only status equality omitted: four accepted and 252 rejected.

The finite enumeration includes every stated status and resolution value. Fixed valid timestamps and response identifiers represent presence classes; omitted versus explicit-null optional metadata is equivalent for the relevant Python checks. Other payload dimensions cannot defeat the implication while the stated validity guards hold.
